key_insight: APPO moves branching and credit assignment from coarse tool-call boundaries to fine-grained decision points, improving agentic RL by identifying which intermediate tokens actually affect outcomes.
engineering_relevance: This makes multi-turn LLM agents more sample-efficient and interpretable, with better tool-use performance without sacrificing efficiency.
method: Branching Score combines token uncertainty with policy-induced likelihood gains to choose where to explore.
Procedure-level advantage scaling spreads credit across branched rollouts at the sequence level.
Branching is done at fine-grained decision points rather than fixed workflows or tool-call boundaries.
evidence_signal: Across 13 benchmarks, APPO improves strong agentic RL baselines by nearly 4 points while maintaining efficient tool-calls and interpretability.
watch_item: Branching at fine-grained sequence positions may increase implementation complexity and requires careful tuning so high-entropy but uninformative tokens are not over-selected.
